Senses.Explanation: “Bodhi originally has no tree” is Huineng’s first verse line, preserved as a quoted case-line and repeatedly appraised in later encounters. Two transmissions explicitly assign the line to Huineng and preserve it with the mirror, nothing-at-all, and dust lines. Daguan Tanying raises both Shenxiu’s and Huineng’s verses, then refuses to treat either as a final possession; Yulin Tongxiu reuses Huineng’s line as an answer to “the phrase without.” The entry therefore preserves an attributed, repeatable case-line. It does not turn the line into a free-standing definition of bodhi or decide the patriarchs’ appraisals.
